candidate_relations.reason: Autoimmune myopericarditis assigns an incompatible immune cause relative to monkeypox/Lyme infection.
Echovirus myocarditis is a related viral myocarditis with incompatible virus; serology was negative.
Syphilis is a historical treated infection and a competing STI, not the reference composite.
Disseminated HSV is a vesicular differential; HSV serologies were negative for acute infection.
Acute coronary syndrome is excluded by normal coronary CT and myopericarditis MRI.
IRIS is unlikely with long-standing undetectable HIV and high CD4.
Coxsackievirus B myocarditis is a classic viral myocarditis with negative serology here.
Disseminated gonococcal infection does not explain myopericarditis and sinus pauses.
Myocarditis is a cardiac-inflammation parent missing pericardial involvement, monkeypox/Lyme, and conduction disease.
Sick sinus syndrome describes the sinus pauses, a conduction manifestation rather than the infectious myopericarditis.
Syphilitic aortitis or coronary disease is an incompatible late-syphilis vascular diagnosis; coronaries were normal.
Lymphoma is not suggested by this acute febrile vesicular myopericarditis.
Syphilitic aortitis or coronary disease again names the wrong syphilitic complication.
Myopericarditis is the cardiac object missing monkeypox etiology, Lyme coinfection, and conduction-system involvement.
Toxoplasmosis-associated myocarditis is a different opportunistic myocarditis, unlikely with CD4 1184.
Endocarditis is not supported by the MRI myopericarditis pattern.
HIV-associated cardiomyopathy is a chronic myocardial disease, incompatible with this acute myopericarditis in suppressed HIV.
